stem: Which of the following best describes how the mean and the median of the counts change when the 11th count is included?
stimulus: An ecologist counted oak seedlings in 10 square plots on a forest floor. The counts were 8, 4, 11, 6, 3, 9, 7, 4, 8, and 5. A storm later opened a gap in the canopy, and an 11th plot inside the gap had 56 seedlings. The ecologist added that count to the data set.
choices: The mean and the median each increase by 4.5.
The mean increases by 4.5, and the median increases by 0.5.
The mean increases by 4.5, and the median does not change.
The mean increases by 0.5, and the median increases by 4.5.
explanation: The first 10 counts add to 65, so their mean is 6.5. Sorted, they are 3, 4, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 8, 9, 11, so the median is $\frac{6+7}{2} = 6.5$. With 56 included, the sum is 121 and the mean is $\frac{121}{11} = 11$, which is an increase of 4.5. With 11 values, the median is the 6th value in sorted order, which is 7. That is an increase of only 0.5. The extreme value pulls the mean up a lot, but it moves the median only one position.

A.why: You found how much the mean changed and assumed the median changed by the same amount. The outlier moves the median only one position in the sorted list, from 6.5 to 7.

C.why: You remembered that an outlier barely moves the median and stopped there without checking the middle value. With 10 values, the median is the average of 6 and 7. With 11 values, it is 7 itself, so the median does change, by 0.5.

D.why: You got the two changes right but swapped them. The mean is the measure that the extreme value pulls hard. The median is the one that barely moves.

stem: Which of the following statements must be true?
stimulus:
A folklorist recorded how many distinct motifs appear in each tale in two collections of trickster stories. The table summarizes the distribution for each collection.

Motifs per Tale
Collection | Minimum | First quartile | Median | Third quartile | Maximum
A | 2 | 5 | 8 | 11 | 20
B | 4 | 6 | 7 | 9 | 12
choices: The mean of collection A is greater than the mean of collection B.
The mean number of motifs per tale in collection A is 8.
The interquartile range of A is less than that of B.
The median of collection A is greater than the median of collection B.
explanation: The table gives each collection's median directly: 8 motifs for A and 7 for B. Since $8 > 7$, the median of collection A is greater. A five-number summary gives no information about the means, so no claim about either mean must be true.

A.why: You inferred the means from a summary that shows only the minimum, the quartiles, the median and the maximum. Collection A's mean could be greater than B's, but nothing in the table guarantees it, so the statement doesn't have to be true.

B.why: You took collection A's median of 8 to be its mean. The table reports medians, not means, and with a maximum of 20 the mean could be well away from 8.

C.why: You reversed the comparison. Collection A's interquartile range is $11 - 5 = 6$ and collection B's is $9 - 6 = 3$, so A's is greater, not less.

stem: Which studio's edition sizes have the greatest mean?
stimulus:
Three printmaking studios each record the edition size (the number of impressions pulled) for their recent prints. The table shows how many prints at each studio had each edition size.

Number of Prints by Edition Size
Edition size | Studio X | Studio Y | Studio Z
10 | 1 | 3 | 1
20 | 3 | 3 | 2
30 | 5 | 2 | 3
40 | 3 | 3 | 4
50 | 1 | 3 | 5
choices: Studio X
Studio Y
Studio Z
All three are equal
explanation: The frequencies for Studio X (1, 3, 5, 3, 1) and Studio Y (3, 3, 2, 3, 3) are symmetric about an edition size of 30, so each of those means is exactly 30. Studio Z's frequencies rise toward the larger edition sizes, so its mean is pulled above 30: $\frac{10 + 40 + 90 + 160 + 250}{15} = \frac{550}{15} \approx 36.7$. Studio Z has the greatest mean.

A.why: You picked the studio with the tallest single frequency, which is 5 prints with an edition size of 30. That describes the mode. Studio X's data are symmetric about 30, so its mean is 30 and no higher.

B.why: You noticed that Studio Y's data are the most spread out and treated that as a larger center. Spread and center are different. Studio Y is symmetric about 30, so its mean is 30.

D.why: You saw that all three studios use the same edition sizes and assumed the means must match. That only holds when each set of frequencies is symmetric about 30. Studio Z's frequencies lean toward the larger sizes, so its mean is higher.

stem:
Which of the following statements must be true?

I. The mean hardness of the 9 samples is greater than the mean hardness of the original 8 samples.
II. The median hardness of the 9 samples is greater than the median hardness of the original 8 samples.
stimulus: A materials scientist measured the Vickers hardness of 8 samples of a new aluminum alloy. A ninth sample, given a different heat treatment, was then tested. Its hardness was greater than the hardness of every one of the original 8 samples. The scientist added this measurement to the data set.
choices: I only
II only
I and II
Neither I nor II
explanation: The new value is greater than every original value, so it is also greater than their mean. Adding a value above the mean always raises the mean, so statement I must be true. With 8 values, the median is the average of the 4th and 5th values in sorted order. With 9 values, it is the 5th value. If the original 4th and 5th values were equal, the median would not change. Statement II could be true, but it doesn't have to be.

B.why: You switched which measure is sensitive to extreme values. The mean is the measure that a new largest value is guaranteed to raise. The median may stay the same.

C.why: You assumed the median must increase because the mean does. The median moves at most one position, and if the original 4th and 5th values were equal, it doesn't move at all. Statement II is possible but not guaranteed.

D.why: You overlooked the condition that the new sample is harder than every original sample. A value greater than all the others is greater than their mean, so the mean must increase.

stem: Which of the following statements about the streamflow readings is true?
stimulus:
A hydrologist recorded the daily streamflow, in cubic meters per second, at two gauging stations for the same 7 days. A sudden cloudburst upstream of station S occurred on day 2.

Daily Streamflow (cubic meters per second)
Station | Day 1 | Day 2 | Day 3 | Day 4 | Day 5 | Day 6 | Day 7
R | 24 | 20 | 26 | 22 | 23 | 21 | 25
S | 23 | 67 | 17 | 25 | 19 | 24 | 21
choices: Stations R and S have the same mean and the same median.
Station S has both the greater mean and the greater median.
Stations R and S have the same median, and S has the greater mean.
Station S has the greater median, and R and S have the same mean.
explanation: In sorted order, station R's readings are 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 25, 26, so its median is 23 and its mean is $\frac{161}{7} = 23$. Station S's readings are 17, 19, 21, 23, 24, 25, 67, so its median is also 23. Its mean is $\frac{196}{7} = 28$. The single reading of 67 pulls station S's mean up, but the medians stay equal.

A.why: You found the medians correctly but assumed the means must match because the centers look alike. Station S's reading of 67 raises its mean to 28, compared with 23 for station R.

B.why: You probably took the middle value in day order instead of sorting first. Read that way, station S's day 4 reading of 25 looks larger than station R's day 4 reading of 22. After sorting, both medians are 23.

D.why: You swapped the two measures. The outlier changes the mean, not the median. Station S has the greater mean, and the two medians are equal.
